bibl.title: Medical Recipes for All Occasions: A receptarium from Tebtunis? (P.CtYBR inv. 1443)
bibl.seg: Anna Monte, Medical Recipes for All Occasions: A receptarium from Tebtunis? (P.CtYBR inv. 1443).
bibl.note: P. Yale Inv. 1443. End of the 1st - early 2nd century. The receptarium, which may originate from the medical milieu of Tebtunis and its temple library, collects recipes for disparate ailments, which have been recorded apparently without a uniform organizing criterion. - Col. II had partly been published by: Ann Ellis Hanson, Greek Medical Papyri from the Fayum Village of Tebtunis: Patient Involvement in a Local Health-Care System?, Hippocrates in Context. Papers read at the XIth International Hippocrates Colloquium. University of Newcastle upon Tyne, 27-31 August 2002 (Leiden, 2005) pp. 387-402.
